<h>Lectio 1</h>
De Isaía Prophéta
<r>Is 26:17-21</r>
<n>17</n> Sicut quæ cóncipit, cum appropinquáverit ad partum, dolens clamat in dolóribus suis: sic facti sumus a fácie tua Dómine.
<n>18</n> Concépimus, et quasi parturívimus, et pepérimus spíritum: salútes non fécimus in terra, ídeo non cecidérunt habitatóres terræ.
<n>19</n> Vivent mórtui tui, interfécti mei resúrgent: expergiscímini, et laudáte qui habitátis in púlvere: quia ros lucis ros tuus, et terram gigántum détrahes in ruínam.

<r>℟.</r> Ecce véniet Dóminus, protéctor noster, Sanctus Israël,
* Corónam regni habens in cápite suo.
<r>℣.</r> Et dominábitur a mari usque ad mare, et a flúmine usque ad términos orbis terrárum.
<r>℟.</r> Corónam regni habens in cápite suo.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the book of Isaias
<r>Is 26:17-21</r>
<n>17</n> As a woman with child, when she draweth near the time of her delivery, is in pain, and crieth out in her pangs: so are we become in thy presence, O Lord.
<n>18</n> We have conceived, and been as it were in labour, and have brought forth wind: we have not wrought salvation on the earth, therefore the inhabitants of the earth have not fallen.
<n>19</n> Thy dead men shall live, my slain shall rise again: awake, and give praise, ye that dwell in the dust: for thy dew is the dew of the light: and the land of the giants thou shalt pull down into ruin.

<r>℟.</r> Behold, there cometh the Lord, our defender, the Holy One of Israel,
* Wearing a royal crown upon His head.
<r>℣.</r> And His dominion shall be from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth.
<r>℟.</r> Wearing a royal crown upon His head.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Is 26:20-21</r>
<n>20</n> Vade pópulus meus, intra in cubícula tua, claude óstia tua super te, abscóndere módicum ad moméntum, donec pertránseat indignátio.
<n>21</n> Ecce enim Dóminus egrediétur de loco suo, ut vísitet iniquitátem habitatóris terræ contra eum: et revelábit terra sánguinem suum, et non opériet ultra interféctos suos.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Sicut mater consolátur fílios suos, ita consolábor vos, dicit Dóminus: et de Ierúsalem civitáte quam elégi, véniet vobis auxílium, et vidébitis,
* Et gaudébit cor vestrum.
<r>℣.</r> Dabo in Sion salútem, et in Ierúsalem glóriam meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et gaudébit cor vestrum.

b.fe0015f287:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>T</c>értio Idus Decémbris Luna tértia décima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>R</h>omæ sancti Dámasi Primi, Papæ et Confessóris; qui Apollinárem hæresiárcham damnávit, et Petrum, Epíscopum Alexandrínum, fugátum restítuit; multa étiam sanctórum Mártyrum córpora invénit, eorúmque memórias vérsibus exornávit.
<h>I</h>tem Romæ pássio sancti Trasónis, qui, cum Christiános laborántes in thermis, aliísque opéribus públicis fatigátos, et in cárcere pósitos, de suis facultátibus áleret, iussu Maximiáni tentus est, et cum áliis duóbus, id est Pontiáno et Prætextáto, martýrio coronátus.
<h>A</h>mbiáni, in Gállia, sanctórum Mártyrum Victórici et Fusciáni, sub eódem Imperatóre, in quorum náribus et áuribus iussit Rictiovárus Præses immítti tarínchas, et clavis ardéntibus témpora transfígi, deínde óculos evélli, ac póstmodum eórum córpora iaculári; sicque, una cum sancto Gentiáno, eórum hóspite, capítibus amputátis, migravérunt ad Dóminum.
<h>I</h>n Pérside sancti Bársabæ Mártyris.
<h>I</h>n Hispánia sancti Eutýchii Mártyris.
<h>P</h>lacéntiæ sancti Sabíni Epíscopi, miráculis clari.
<h>C</h>onstantinópoli sancti Daniélis Stylítæ.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.6396f21a96:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>D</c>ecember 11th 2027, the 13th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:

<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy Confessor Pope Damasus (of Spain), who condemned the arch-heretic Apollinaris, and restored to his papacy Peter, Pope of Alexandria, who had been driven into exile moreover, he found the bodies of many holy martyrs, and caused to be engraved upon their tombstones verses composed by himself. (He died in the year 384.)
<h>L</h>ikewise at Rome, the holy martyr Thrason, who fed at his own expense Christians who were in prison or sent to work in the baths, or at other public works. He was arrested by order of the Emperor Maximian, and crowned with martyrdom along with two others named Pontian and Pretextatus, (about the year 293.)
<h>A</h>t Amiens, under the same Emperor Maximian, the holy martyrs Victoricus and Fuscian. Rictiovarus the President had iron spikes driven into their nostrils and ears, and redhot nails hammered into their temples after which their eyes were torn out, their bodies pierced with darts, and their heads cut off, and so they and holy Gentian, their host, passed away to be for ever with the Lord, (in the year 303.)
<h>(</h>At Astrahara, near Persepolis,) in Persia, the holy martyr Barsabas, (with ten monks, whose Abbot he was, in the year 342, at the beginning of the great persecution under Sapor II.)
<h>I</h>n Spain, the holy martyr Eutychius.
<h>A</h>t Piacenza, holy Sabinus, Bishop of that see, (in the fourth century,) famous for miracles.
<h>A</h>t Constantinople, (about the year 489,) holy Daniel the Stylite.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
